title: Email's @ came from a rarely used key
body: In 1971 Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email between two machines at BBN. He needed a character separating user from host that could not appear in names, and picked @ from the teletype keyboard. The machines, incidentally, stood side by side; the network was the point.
source_hint: BBN / Internet Hall of Fame, Tomlinson 1971
